precepts.text: How long shall it be to the end of these wonders? A time, times, and an half: a time is a hundred years, times is two hundred, and an half: 350 years, and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people. Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed: we forgot who we are, we even forgot our nationality. After 70 AD our country was destroyed, but we still built cities in Africa, still had kings and governments, still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power was scattered.
precepts.point: Without the ephod: no priest there to guide you and tell you what God needs you to do. That's the religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance stripped away.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
Hosea says the children of Israel “shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod”. Daniel 12 gives the time frame for it. “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?” The wonders are our people being destroyed, enslaved and colonized, being without a king, without a prince, without an ephod.

“it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is a hundred years; times is two hundred, three hundred in all; and an half makes 350 years. “and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.” Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed. All that power was gone from us; we forgot who we are, and we even forgot our nationality.

When we fled Jerusalem in 70 AD, was our power destroyed? Our country was destroyed, but we went to Africa and built cities there, and the ten tribes were set up on this side of the world doing their thing too. We still had governments, we still had kings over us, and we still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power of the holy people was scattered.

That is the many days without a king: without political sovereignty, when Europe colonized Ghana, Nigeria, Angola, Senegal, Papua New Guinea and the Congo, and when the transatlantic slave trade took us. It is without an image: our minds destroyed until the sisters in Africa bleach their skin and put on weaves, because worshipping the God of your oppressor destroys the way you look at yourself. The same curses fell on our people all over Africa, like the Mau Mau in Kenya, tortured in British camps and paid less than 4,000 pounds each. That is why I don't want no damn reparations.

precepts.point: Without the ephod: no priest there to guide you and tell you what God needs you to do. That's the religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance stripped away.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
Daniel 12 gives the time frame for when our people would be without a king, without an image, and without a sacrifice, as Hosea 3:4 says. Verse 11 reads: “And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.”

The daily sacrifice taken away is Hosea's “without a sacrifice”. Without the sacrifice, the image and the ephod, all our religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance was stripped away, and there was no priest to guide us and tell us what God needs us to do. The white man came in, whipped us, taught us white Jesus and his lies, and forced it down our throats in Africa. After he brought the slaves over here, he went to Africa and destroyed them there, until the people in Africa don't even know that we in the Caribbean and America are the same people.

So from the taking away of the sacrifice, the days are counted, and the question Daniel asked, “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?”, is answered with a set time. That goes back to the yoke of iron upon thy neck until thou have been destroyed: it did not just happen to us over here, it happened to our people in Africa, and the scattering of the holy people runs its appointed course.

precepts.text: Many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. When you die you go to sleep, yes; but Christ has the power to wake you up: some to everlasting life, and some to shame.
precepts.point: The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us. What was just went over is a secret thing that Moses understood: he understood we would be brought into spiritual Egypt, into America, and he saw America destroyed.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
Christ has the power over life and death, which is why Daniel 12 says some shall awake. “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Many of them are going to awake. Some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. When you die, you go to sleep, yes. But Christ has the power to wake your behind up and torment you.

That is what stands behind the carcases of Isaiah 66:24, whose worm does not die and whose fire is not quenched, and behind the land of Deuteronomy 29 that is all brimstone, salt and burning. Those who forsook the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers and served other gods do not simply die and disappear: they are awakened to shame and everlasting contempt. As 2 Esdras 9 says, read in the same moment, those who despised his law while the place of repentance was open “must know it after death by pain.” And the righteous awake to everlasting life, the seed and the name that remain.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Daniel says “there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered”. What makes this tribulation different is World War III and Armageddon, and Psalm 91 shows how Israel is delivered in the midst of it.

“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” The secret place of the Most High is the Bible.

“Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” The arrow that flieth by day is the missile, the destruction that wasteth at noonday.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” And “he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.”

That is the deliverance of the Israelites in the midst of Armageddon: thy people delivered, every one found written in the book, not all nations. It is the same psalm Satan twisted when he told Christ to jump from the pinnacle of the temple.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Daniel's “time of trouble, such as never was” is World War III and Armageddon. Ezra shows it: “And there shall be great fearfulness and trembling upon earth: and they that see the wrath shall be afraid, and trembling shall come upon them.”

“And then shall there come great storms from the south, and from the north, and another part from the west. And strong winds shall arise from the east”: storms from all four winds.

They “shall pour out over every high and eminent place an horrible star, Fire, and hail, and flying swords”. The horrible star is the ICBM, and the flying swords are the missiles. “And they shall break down the cities and walls, mountains and hills, trees of the wood, and grass of the meadows, and their corn.”

“And they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid.” Babylon is America. And “then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her”, just as Revelation 18 says the kings and merchants of the earth will bewail her. That is the time of trouble in which Daniel's people, every one written in the book, shall be delivered.

precepts.why:
Psalm 91 promises the deliverance of Israel in the time of trouble: “He shall give his angels charge over thee”. Satan used that same psalm on Christ: “And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence”.

“For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee: And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.” Satan twisted the psalm into a dare, telling Christ to jump.

“And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.” Christ answered that way because the psalm is not a dare to test God. It is about the deliverance of Israel in the midst of Armageddon, when a thousand fall at our side and ten thousand at our right hand, and the angels bear us up.

precepts.why:
Daniel says “at that time thy people shall be delivered”. John shows the order of it: “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” That standing up is now.

“And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.” Between the standing up and the deliverance, John left out the tribulation, World War III and Armageddon; the precepts supply it. Tribulation has to come, then World War III, then Armageddon, when Christ comes in the midst of World War III.

“And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven.” A great destruction.

The Israelites who want to invest in airplanes and boats to get out do not believe the angels are coming. Come up hither is the deliverance: the angels bear us up, as Psalm 91 says.

precepts.point: Because thou hast kept the word of my patience I will keep thee from the hour of temptation which shall come upon all the world: Jacob's trouble leading into World War III and Armageddon. No force field; they are at rest. The righteous perisheth and no man layeth it to heart, but merciful men are taken away from the evil to come; they enter into peace and rest in their beds, each walking in his uprightness, and many that sleep in the dust shall awake. That is why when brothers and sisters die I do not do the tears.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Isaiah 57 says the righteous “shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness”: they are not dead. Daniel 12 says the same thing.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”. Those that sleep in the dust are the ones that died, and they shall awake, “some to everlasting life”: the righteous brothers and the righteous sisters; “and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

“And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.”

So the saints who died keeping the word of Christ’s patience are only sleeping. They were kept from the hour of temptation that comes upon all the world, Jacob’s trouble, and they will awake to everlasting life. That is why we do not grieve the righteous the way the world does.

precepts.text: Michael shall stand up for the children of thy people, and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book. Israel is written in the book of life, not everybody. Jeremiah 46:28: fear thou not, O Jacob, for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee, but I will not make a full end of thee; I will correct thee in measure, yet not leave thee wholly unpunished. 2 Esdras 9:22: let the multitude perish which was born in vain, and let my grape be kept, for with great labour have I made it perfect.

Jeremiah 51:49: as Babylon hath caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth. Revelation 18:24: in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth. The judgment on this kingdom will be the worst of all.

note.label: War & the Pain of Repentance

precepts.why:
Revelation 20 says whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire. So who is written in the book of life? Is it the Chinese, the white man, or the Arabs? Daniel answers.

“And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time.” That is the indignation of Isaiah 26, when God's people must “enter thou into thy chambers” and hide “until the indignation be overpast.” There will be so much devastation that we will be fearful.

“And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” Who is written in the book of life? Israel, Daniel's people. Not everybody.

Jeremiah says the same, and they hate this one: “Fear thou not, O Jacob my servant, saith the Lord: for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure; yet will I not leave thee wholly unpunished.” God is correcting us in measure, but he will not destroy us.

And Ezra: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain; and let my grape be kept, and my plant; for with great labour have I made it perfect.” All the nations were born in vain; the Israelites are the grape and the plant that is kept. So when the Lord comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth, Israel written in the book is delivered, and all the nations go into the lake of fire.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.” Daniel saw the same two resurrections: “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Some to everlasting life, some to shame and everlasting contempt: the resurrection of life and the resurrection of damnation. “The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live.” That happened before their eyes with Lazarus, and it reaches forward to the last judgment, when all that are in the graves hear his voice and awake, as Daniel wrote.
